issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What and why

FrontierScience tests whether a model can write a scientific answer and earn credit for its reasoning. **Olympiad** checks short answers in physics, chemistry, and biology against a reference. **Research** awards up to 10 points for steps in a written solution, with a pass at 7. Both tracks use a single turn. This issue covers implementation and validation. ID policy admission and EvalDash presentation are separate decisions. [Implementation PR #11887](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11887) · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1) · [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/tree/25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30)

### Pilot results

The release contains 100 Olympiad and 60 Research questions. Fractions below give correct or passing answers over **graded questions**. The final column shows partial credit even when a Research answer fell short of passing.

| Solver | Olympiad correct / graded | Research passed / graded | Mean Research points / 10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPT-4o | 12/100 | 0/59 | 1.60 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 69/100 | 3/58 | 2.41 |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B-IT | 53/99 | 3/58 | 2.18 |
| GPT-OSS-20B | 58/100 | 4/58 | 3.38 |

GPT-4o scored 12.0% on Olympiad versus OpenAI’s 12.3%. On Research, 0 passes in 59 questions is consistent with OpenAI’s 0.4%. Among the 57 Research rows graded for all three open-weight solvers, GPT-OSS-20B led Qwen and Gemma by one pass. [GPT-4o comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7050505312) · [Shared-row results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7024514371)

### Differences from OpenAI’s evaluation

- **Trials and judge.** OpenAI averaged 20 trials per Olympiad question and 30 per Research question with GPT-5 at high effort. Marin requested one answer per selected question and used GPT-OSS-120B at high effort with the published judge prompts.
- **Solver settings.** Marin used each solver’s own output budget, disabled tools, and graded the visible final answer. A length-limited answer could still earn credit.
- **Coverage.** The adapter includes all 160 released rows. Pilot selections varied by solver, and missing grades are excluded from the denominators above. The headline includes both copies of a duplicated Research question.
- **Grader uncertainty.** GPT-OSS-120B and GPT-5 agreed on 14 of 15 selected Research answers, all 14 below the pass threshold. Two blinded reviewers passed two answers both judges scored below threshold. Those disagreements lack subject-expert adjudication. [Judge comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7019749128)

<details>
<summary>Scores by subject, coverage, uncertainty, and duplicate sensitivity</summary>

Each cell gives correct or passing answers over graded questions. Subject counts are physics, chemistry, biology. SE is in percentage points, stratified by subject and treating the two identical Research questions as a cluster. It describes variation across graded problems. One answer per row cannot estimate variation across repeated runs of the same questions.

| Solver | Track | Graded result | Selected / released | SE | Physics | Chemistry | Biology | Published reference |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GPT-4o | Olympiad | 12/100 | 100/100 | 3.26 | 6/50 | 6/40 | 0/10 | OpenAI 12.3% |
| GPT-4o | Research | 0/59 | 59/60 | 0.00 observed | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0/19 | OpenAI 0.4% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Olympiad | 69/100 | 100/100 | 4.49 | 35/50 | 31/40 | 3/10 | SU-01 65%, Axion 71% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Research | 3/58 | 59/60 | 2.94 | 1/19 | 0/20 | 2/19 | SU-01 5%, Axion 26.7% |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B-IT | Olympiad | 53/99 | 100/100 | 5.02 | 28/50 | 22/39 | 3/10 | — |
| Gemma 4 26B-A4B-IT | Research | 3/58 | 58/60 | 2.93 | 0/20 | 2/20 | 1/18 | — |
| GPT-OSS-20B | Olympiad | 58/100 | 100/100 | 4.91 | 29/50 | 26/40 | 3/10 | — |
| GPT-OSS-20B | Research | 4/58 | 58/60 | 3.41 | 1/20 | 2/20 | 1/18 | — |

Mean Research scores on each solver’s graded rows were 1.60/10 for GPT-4o, 2.41 for Qwen, 2.18 for Gemma and 3.38 for GPT-OSS-20B. On the 99 Olympiad rows graded for all three native solvers, Qwen scored 69, Gemma 53 and GPT-OSS-20B 58. Within the shared native selection, Qwen hit its output limit on 5/100 Olympiad and 1/58 Research answers. Gemma and GPT-OSS-20B had zero length stops among returned answers. GPT-4o had zero on either track. [Native results and token usage](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7024514371) · [Qwen grade recovery](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7018652234)

OpenAI averaged 20 Olympiad trials and 30 Research trials with GPT-5-high judging. Here Together GPT-OSS-120B judged one answer per selected question. GPT-4o used OpenAI’s 2024-11-20 snapshot through OpenRouter. Exact snapshot parity is unverified. Olympiad differs from Figure 6 by −0.3 percentage points. For 0/59, the two-sided 95% exact binomial interval is 0–6.1% under an independent-question approximation. The pilot has little power to distinguish zero from 0.4%. [GPT-4o archive, cost and recoveries](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7050505312)

Qwen used an 81,920-token output cap. Gemma and GPT-OSS-20B used their respective remaining contexts. The three native solvers used thinking where supported, with tool use disabled. Qwen attempted all Research rows except 59 and lacks a grade on row 17. The native follow-ups omitted 50 and 59. GPT-4o omitted 50. The updated pilot selects 59 Research rows. The full adapter includes all 60. Shared-row Qwen/Gemma/GPT-OSS Research counts are 3/57, 3/57 and 4/57. Dropping duplicate row 12 gives 3/56, 3/56 and 4/56. [Protocol decisions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7046268852)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Published comparisons for Qwen</summary>

Two teams published scores for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B baseline. Neither team's exact weights revision has been verified against Marin’s pin.

| Source | Olympiad | Research | How the team reported the score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [SU-01, Tables 1–2](https://huggingface.co/Simplified-Reasoning/SU-01#evaluation) | 65.0% | 5.0% | Olympiad averages four runs. SU-01 describes rule-based checks followed by GPT-OSS-120B for unresolved Olympiad answers, and GPT-5-high for Research. Research repeat count is unverified. [Grading details, Appendix G](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13301v1#A7) |
| [ByteDance Axion, §4.1 and Table 2](https://axion1-0.github.io/paper/axion.pdf) | 71.0% | 26.7% | Best complete run of three. The harness supports tools under benchmark-specific restrictions. Qwen’s actual tool use on these tracks is unverified. |

The 21.7-point gap on Research makes either aggregate a weak test of grader correctness. Where reference grades are available, compare verdicts on the same saved answers.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Protocol decisions, solver settings, and length stops</summary>

| Decision | OpenAI’s published evaluation | Marin pilot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Population | The gold set has 100 Olympiad and 60 Research rows. The paper does not say how its runner handled the duplicate Research problem. | The adapter includes all released rows. Report correct or passing answers over graded rows, selection coverage over the release, and shared-row comparisons. Count both duplicate copies in the headline and show the effect of removing row 12. |
| Trials | OpenAI averaged accuracy over 20 independent trials per Olympiad question and 30 per Research question. | Generate one response per row. Report a standard error across problems for each track, preserving subject mix and grouping the duplicate Research rows during resampling. One draw per row cannot measure run-to-run variation on the fixed release. |
| Solver | Reasoning models used high effort, except GPT-5.2 at xhigh. Browsing was disabled. We found no numeric solver output cap in the release. | Send the released problem in one user turn, with thinking enabled and no tools or retrieval. Qwen’s thinking switch has no established equivalence to OpenAI’s effort levels. |
| Judge and scores | GPT-5 at high effort checked answer equivalence for Olympiad and awarded rubric points for Research. Research passes at **7/10 or above**. | Use GPT-OSS-120B at high effort with the published Appendix B prompts. Give the judge the problem, visible final answer, and reference answer or rubric. Report Olympiad accuracy and Research pass rate separately. Also retain decimal rubric points and report their mean. |

For the full Qwen3.6-35B-A3B run, set the output cap to **81,920 tokens**, shared between reasoning and the final answer. Qwen recommends this cap for highly complex benchmarks independently of thinking mode. The SU-01 evaluation setup lists 131K tokens for Olympiad and 256K for Research. Record length stops by track so reviewers can judge whether the cap affected scores. [Qwen guidance](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B#best-practices) · [SU-01 evaluation settings](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13301v1)

Use Qwen’s general-task thinking preset on both full tracks: `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=1.5`, and `repetition_penalty=1.0`. Equivalence to OpenAI’s original sampling settings is unverified. [Qwen model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B#best-practices)

For a solver length stop, grade the visible final-answer text. A correct Olympiad answer can earn full credit. A partial Research solution earns the rubric points it satisfies and passes at 7/10. Score zero if the solver produces no final-answer text. Keep length stops in the denominator and report them separately. Marin’s ID OlympiadBench scorer provides precedent for accepting a complete extractable answer when generation reaches its limit. Final-only extraction and partial Research rubric credit are explicit FrontierScience pilot choices. [ID policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) · [Pinned OlympiadBench scorer](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/chat_benchmarks/OlympiadBench/eval_instruct.py#L568-L581)

Set `EvaluationItem.groups["subject"]` from the source row so the run records contain both track headline scores and six subject scores, one for each track and subject. Pool graded rows for each headline and show the graded counts by subject. In this issue, link the run records and show the correct or passing count, graded count, and expected population alongside each score. Verify coverage with `cli scores`. [Subject reporting, Figure 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1#S3.SS1) · [Marin subgroup reporting](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/139b752890/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md#L130-L138)

See [published settings and aggregation, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1#S3.SS1) · [judge prompt, Appendix B](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/2fcd284c-b468-4c21-8ee0-7a783933efcc/frontierscience-paper.pdf) · [dataset discussion of the duplicate](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/discussions/3).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Grader audit, malformed verdicts, and missing answers</summary>

Two independent blinded gpt-6.2-astra reviewers at medium effort scored 19 Qwen answers, including one missing-grade diagnostic. Both passed Research rows 21 and 28 where both GPT judges leaned fail. Comparing GPT-OSS-120B with GPT-5-high gave 14/15 matching classifications on the graded physics and chemistry subset, all failures. Three additional unblinded biology spot checks on saved GPT-4o Olympiad answers bring the inspected graded count to 21. Row 92 omitted circularity from the single-stranded form, row 95 named UMAP in the final line but discussed batch effects earlier, and row 96 named autophagy instead of N-glycan biosynthesis. All scored incorrect. Rows 92 and 95 illustrate sensitivity to specificity and final-answer wording. The three spot checks do not extend the blinded agreement estimate. [Blinded audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7018855152)

Across the six native archives, all eight original Research “single verdict” parser failures ended in a bold Markdown verdict (Gemma rows 4, 30, 53 and GPT-OSS-20B rows 3, 17, 20, including retries). Qwen row 17 also returned bold verdicts in judge-only recovery after its original judge hit the token cap. GPT-4o's archived malformed retry on Research row 1 showed the same pattern. Its initial harness retained the error messages but did not persist the initial malformed replies for rows 1 and 6. Gemma Olympiad row 90 has no saved solver answer. Missing grades remain outside the scored denominator. [GPT-4o recovery](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7050505312)

The two GPT judges differed by 0.72 rubric points on average in absolute terms. Each differed from the blinded reviewers by 1.27–1.68 points. These figures describe 15 selected physics and chemistry answers. Expert adjudication of disputed grades remains a limitation. [Frozen-answer judge comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11691#issuecomment-7019749128)

A separate CPU audit with a simulated judge confirmed all 160 rendered judge prompts matched the Axion templates. Of 47 synthetic verdicts, the 15 scored by Marin received the same reward from Axion. Marin treated the remaining 32 as infrastructure errors, including 24 Axion would score. This measures parser behavior. The audit also compared 43 other benchmark cases and documented integration checks for two concurrent judge PRs. [Grader audit at 6178abdce](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11887#issuecomment-7077100869)

</details>

### Corpus and execution checks

All 160 compiled prompts, references or rubrics, and subject labels matched the pinned release.

<details>
<summary>Pilot branch, source checks, restart test, and archived run records</summary>

The implementation PR registers the full Olympiad and Research tracks and adds decimal Research scoring. The preserved pilot branch contains the launcher, Qwen settings, explicit row selection, and additional judge request and usage logging used for the pilot. The per-solver coverage above describes the historical runs. [Pilot branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/frontierscience-pilot-11691) · [Launcher at the pinned commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ab1a63429b18140926662ab2b91fe98184da063b/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/frontierscience/pilot.py) · [Qwen configuration at the pinned commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ab1a63429b18140926662ab2b91fe98184da063b/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/frontierscience/Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.yaml)

The validation bundle contains native CLI score output for six runs, source record URIs, recovered per-row metrics, uncertainty calculations, and the retained failure inventory. `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/ablations/frontierscience-validation-11691/ccb9e7b84db17214044889db5c27c70c2ec89a4fa4ab7f35e1686a46928c9792.tar.gz` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fevals%2Fablations%2Ffrontierscience-validation-11691%2Fccb9e7b84db17214044889db5c27c70c2ec89a4fa4ab7f35e1686a46928c9792.tar.gz)

**Source checked.** The dataset card lists Apache-2.0. At revision `25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30`, Olympiad contains 50 physics, 40 chemistry, and 10 biology rows. [Pinned Olympiad file](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/blob/25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30/olympiad/test.jsonl)

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

No open PR targets FrontierScience. TaskCompendium derives task IDs from source provenance, including the row locator, so the duplicate Research rows can retain separate execution identities. Three requested Qwen sampling fields are absent from the evaluation protocol, the current Qwen3.6 serve config has a 32,768-token context, and Verifyit's judge has no continuous 0–10 rubric score; these require implementation before the full pilot.

**Relevant code**
- [Task ID derivation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4e4a35f8ae68a8a5a76626f2f323f16dabbd881d/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/conversion.py#L37) — includes the source row.
- [Evaluation protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4e4a35f8ae68a8a5a76626f2f323f16dabbd881d/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/spec.py#L162) — sampling and metrics contract.
- [Request serialization](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4e4a35f8ae68a8a5a76626f2f323f16dabbd881d/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L115) — sends current sampling fields.
- [Judge contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4e4a35f8ae68a8a5a76626f2f323f16dabbd881d/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/spec.py#L314) — fixed labels and checklist scoring.
- [Qwen serve config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4e4a35f8ae68a8a5a76626f2f323f16dabbd881d/experiments/evaluation/serve/models/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.yaml#L1) — current context limit.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add source converters for `olympiad/test.jsonl` and `research/test.jsonl` at revision `25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30`, with separate benchmark declarations. Preserve each released row's locator and original task ID in evidence; set `groups["subject"]`, `final_only` response selection, one trial, and independent headline metrics. Register both in the curated catalog. Test the 100/60 populations, subject counts, and two independent Research duplicate IDs and grades through resume.
2. Reproduce the Appendix B judge prompts. Implement Olympiad equivalence on the judge path; add a strictly parsed decimal 0–10 Research score that records rubric points and a pass at `>=7`. Keep malformed judge output as a grading failure and an empty solver final answer as scored zero. Bind GPT-OSS-120B with high reasoning effort and retain the returned model identity and judge budget.
3. Represent `min_p`, presence penalty, and repetition penalty in the typed sampling contract and outgoing request. Verify the full Qwen payload, including `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, thinking enabled, and the 81,920-token output cap. Pin the Qwen checkpoint and set serving context from the longest rendered prompt plus that cap; require context admission to preserve the full allowance.
4. Build both full corpora locally and compare solver and judge prompts with the pinned source and Appendix B. Test score boundaries below, at, and above 7, length stops, malformed verdicts, request fields, and duplicate-row restart behavior. Smoke 50 rows per track with Qwen3-0.6B; proceed only after `cli scores` shows 50 graded rows on each track without infrastructure failures.
5. Run all 100 and 60 rows on the pinned Qwen3.6 checkpoint. Report both headline scores, six subject scores, mean Research rubric points, expected/graded counts, length stops, judge failures, standard errors, and the 59-problem sensitivity score. Audit at least 20 saved grades plus every malformed case, including two blinded reviewers on the same saved sample. Publish run links and reference comparisons in a validation PR using the `manage-pr` issue-fixes workflow with `Fixes #11691`.

issues.title: [eval] Implement both FrontierScience tracks with separate scores

issues.author: znichols
issues.body:
## Goal

Produce the **first 10,000 accepted science RL tasks**, starting with computational-biology environments built from independently sourced, openly licensed data of the kind that supports BixBench-like analysis. This issue tracks **our task production**, not RL Atlas development; submit a task to RL Atlas only after it is rights-cleared and validated. Aim for distinct, executable analysis programs across genuinely independent source families—not paraphrases, changed thresholds, multiple model seeds, or benchmark questions.

A **bucket** is one source document or a coherent group of source documents/data files for a study. Record the bucket's source family, pinned manifest, rights and privacy evidence, the exact input projection, candidate analysis programs, TaskForge IDs, validation outcomes, and Atlas submission. A downloaded record is not automatically an independent bucket or a usable environment.

## Pipeline and counting rules

1. **Identified:** Find a plausible source bucket or family. Record study relationships, declared licenses, sensitivity flags and a file inventory. A search hit is not a cleared bucket.
2. **Archived:** Pin and checksum source bytes, selection and manifest immutably. Archive bytes are *never* automatically generator or solver inputs.
3. **Test extracted:** Run a small, bounded task-extraction/analysis pilot from source-only context; verify the relevant fields, units, joins and candidate computations. Three real-data buckets have one independently executed provisional analysis each. A schema/header probe alone does not count.
4. **Fully extracted:** Complete **all task extraction planned for that bucket under a stated, bounded extraction plan**, including attempts, explicit no-task/failed outcomes and a frozen candidate/disposition ledger. A completed *wave* says nothing about whether more task families could ever be mined; a new expanded plan needs its own version. **This phase is about task extraction, not licensing or solver-input projection.**
5. **TaskForged:** Turn the extracted candidate tasks into actual TaskForge TaskSpecs with deterministic graders, full keyset/answer contracts and negative controls. A model-produced idea or grader plan does not count. This label means *built*, not accepted for RL.
6. **Characterized:** Run fresh-agent solver trials, grader adversaries (including missing/extra/duplicate keys and plausible wrong methods), independent scientific/reference checks and private published-result/eval overlap review. Record difficulty, failures, Stage 50 evidence and a Stage 60 decision. Characterization may quarantine or reject a task.
7. **Landed:** Submit only rights-cleared, Stage 60-accepted tasks to RL Atlas with provenance, hashes, source-family split and validation evidence. Count toward 10k only here; no benchmark item text, keys, solved notebooks, teacher rollouts or private audits enter generation.

## Inventory: source collections versus individual buckets (2026-11-23)

I previously labeled **acquisition waves** as “buckets”; that was wrong. GTN and Zenodo search rounds are *ways we found material*, not three or four coherent source studies. We have a few **source collections** and **three individually test-extracted real-data buckets**; the 386 deposits still need study-family consolidation. A conditional planning estimate is not a count of tasks.

**Count units matter:** a page, repository, deposit, analysis idea and TaskSpec are different units. The cells below count progress within each *collection*, not individual independent studies. **Fully extracted means the documented, bounded task-extraction plan was finished, not that every conceivable task was found.** Constituent rights/privacy and a minimal hashed solver-input projection are **separate mandatory gates** before exposing real data to a new author/solver or landing tasks; campaign completion does not settle them. The older campaigns ran bounded waves without those gates being fully resolved.

| Source collection | Identified | Archived | Test extracted | Fully extracted | TaskForged | Characterized | Landed | Yield / scope |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| BioTasks notebooks + repositories | **57 documents + 405 repositories** | **57** documents + **405** bounded repo evidence bundles | **57 + 405** processed; 87 notebook ideas and 398 hydrated repo ideas | **57 document + 405 repository dispositions** in completed bounded campaigns (including nulls/hydration failures) | **352 distinct ideas built**: 87 notebook TaskSpecs + 265 repo TaskSpecs; **305** of the 352 selected to the combined campaign (40 + 265) | **0 fully characterized**; 305 had single-GLM diagnostic trials, 230 had 12-model diagnostic trials | **0** | 352 provisional builds, **not** 352 approved tasks; 47 notebook builds were not combined |
| MedlinePlus Genetics + NHGRI | **139 pages** in pinned intake | **139** HTML pages | **126** articles yielded **195** passages; **101** pages contributed to projected tasks | **195 passages** completed the authorized adaptive extraction plan (3,818 attempted arms, 840 model-screened leads, explicit stop/quarantine records) | **630** provisional TaskSpecs with structural/key controls | **0 fully characterized**; 3 had diagnostic solver/control trials | **0** | 630 already built; instructional MCQs, **not** BixBench-like data-analysis tasks |
| GTN + independently discovered Zenodo biology data | **1,156 record IDs** in deduplicated metadata library (*not* study families) | **386 distinct deposits**, 1,924 checksum-verified files | **3 individual source buckets** with verified source-only profiles and independently executed provisional analyses; further header-only probes do not count | **0 buckets** with completed extraction plans | **0** | **0** | **0** | **386–1,158** *hypothetical* analysis slots under an untested 1–3 per independent eligible record assumption; 0 verified tasks |
| nf-core fixture leads | **4 pinned branches** (not four independent studies) | **0 fixture bytes** archived | **0** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **0** | Unknown |

**Actual provisional TaskForge builds: 352 + 630 = 982 distinct ideas** (the combined BioTasks 305 are a *subset* of 352, not an extra cohort); **0 landed tasks**. Of the 982, the curated combined BioTasks snapshot has 305, so **935 = 305 + 630** is the narrower selected-snapshot count. Neither 982 nor 935 is training-cleared. The real-data archive adds **zero TaskForge builds** and only a non-forecast planning range. **770 of 1,156** Zenodo/GTN metadata IDs remain unacquired: **646** small leads in active/manual-review queues plus **124** separately held GTN records. No double-counting across acquisition rounds.

### Individual real-data bucket phase grid

`✓` complete, `·` not complete. Test extraction is a limited source-only task pilot; fully extracted means the bucket's **declared full task-extraction plan is complete**. None of these three has such a plan completed. Rights/privacy and solver projection are separate gates, not phases in this grid. These three are **within** the 386 acquired records.

| Bucket | Identified | Archived | Test extracted | Fully extracted | TaskForged | Characterized | Landed | Executed provisional analyses |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | ---: |
| Plant–pollinator interactions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | 1 |
| Individual plant traits | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | 1 |
| Insect OTU counts | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | 1 |

Other archived records have partial header/file-inventory probes, not completed test extraction. Add a private row **per reviewed source family** as studies are consolidated. Do not make public bucket rows from 386 unreviewed deposits or treat a collection/search wave as one coherent bucket.

### Acquisition pools (not buckets)

Counts below are **records or leads, not accepted buckets**. The downloaded-only planning range assumes *one to three different executable analyses per independently eligible source*, **before** rights, semantic deduplication, projection, grader and solver losses. It is a conditional workload ceiling/range, not a measured forecast; actual accepted yield from these sources is **zero**. The three pilot records are included in the 386 and must not be added again.

| Acquisition pool / leads | Inventory and stage | Conditional analysis slots; accepted tasks | Next gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Three first-pass independent-source buckets**, *subset of cohorts below*: plant–pollinator interactions, individual plant traits, insect OTU counts | Archived; corrected answer-free profiles and **three distinct provisional analyses** each executed by two agreeing private implementations with wrong-method controls. No TaskForge submission. | **3 executed provisional analyses; 0 accepted tasks.** This is not an extra three records in the total. | Constituent rights/privacy, stable allowlisted input projection, real grader and solver/overlap checks. OTU measurement provenance and published-derivative exclusion need particular care. |
| **GTN-linked Zenodo deposits** | **39 downloaded** source-only records (33 initial + six later); metadata discovery included 211 GTN-linked records across 16 topics. Not cleared or semantically deduplicated into studies. | **39–117 hypothetical slots; 0 accepted.** | Review individual file rights, input completeness, source-family overlap and projections. Tutorial/repository licenses do not confer data-file rights. |
| **Earlier independent Zenodo deposits** | **116 downloaded** source-only records in the earlier independent-selection/review waves. Not cleared. | **116–348 hypothetical slots; 0 accepted.** | Constituent rights, sensitive content, file roles, joins, nested assets, projection. |
| **Independent Zenodo discovery, round three** | **121 downloaded** and **236 metadata-only pending**. Downloaded bytes are verified but not cleared. | Downloaded: **121–363 hypothetical slots; 0 accepted**. Pending: **yield unknown**, not 236 usable buckets. | Review files/studies and prioritize bounded acquisition; do not supply descriptions containing study answers to authoring. |
| **Independent Zenodo discovery, round four** | **110 downloaded** and **234 metadata-only pending**; same restrictions. | Downloaded: **110–330 hypothetical slots; 0 accepted**. Pending: **yield unknown**. | Same gates as round three. |
| **Older small metadata leads** | **176 unacquired**: 87 passed only a mechanical metadata screen; 89 held for manual sensitivity, archive/solution or other concerns. | **Unknown; 0 accepted.** Do not promote the 87 automatically. | Manual constituent and privacy review before any acquisition or projection. |
| **nf-core test-data fixtures** | Four pinned branches (`rnaseq`, `ampliseq`, `viralrecon`, `mag`) inventoried without copying fixture bytes. A branch/file is not a study bucket. | **Unknown; 0 accepted.** | Trace each fixture's data provenance, rights and relation to other buckets. |

**Combined acquired inventory:** **386 distinct records**, **1,924 verified files**, **2,593,708,509 bytes (~2.59 GB)**, with **386–1,158 conditional analysis slots** under the untested one-to-three assumption. A manifest hash/normalized-title audit does not prove independent study families. Four records contain nested archives. **Unacquired small leads:** 176 + 236 + 234 = **646**, with unknown yield. None of these cohorts is a 1,000–2,000 credible *usable-task* pool yet. Even if every qualifying source supplied three accepted tasks, 10k would require at least **3,334 independent usable families**; scale source discovery and validated program diversity rather than multiplying shallow variants.

**Existing-campaign caveat:** BioTasks' selected 305 have reference disputes and rights/release gates; its other 47 notebook TaskSpecs were excluded from that selected set. MedlinePlus/NHGRI's 630 passed structural preflight but page-rights and biology review remain, and three had only diagnostic solver/control trials. None is training-cleared. Benchmark archives and the 20-capsule profiling pilot's **96 unverified seeds** are **not source buckets**; original eval tasks, solutions and notebooks never enter generation.

**Per-bucket ledger to maintain from here:** `bucket_id | source_family_id | pinned_source_manifest | identified_at | archived_at | test_extracted_at | extraction_plan_id + planned distinct programs + stop rule | fully_extracted_at + candidate/no-task dispositions | taskforged_at | characterized_at + verdict | landed_at + Atlas IDs | separate constituent-rights/privacy verdict | solver_projection_sha256 | conditional/actual task yield | next blocker`. Merge deposits from one study under a single family; a disposition or `0` is a valid outcome. Keep audit-only identities and restricted details in the private ledger, not the public issue or generator context.

## Immediate milestones

- [ ] For the **three executable pilot analyses**, settle constituent-file rights/privacy and publish private, hash-pinned *allowlisted* solver projections (archive and private references remain inaccessible to solver/author).
- [ ] Implement TaskForge proposal sources and deterministic full-key graders for those three; test adversarial missing/extra/duplicate keys, numerical boundaries, malformed answers and plausible wrong methods.
- [ ] Run fresh-agent solver trials, independent biology and published-result checks, and private eval-overlap review. Record Stage 50/60 evidence or quarantine each task.
- [ ] Review more *independent* interaction, trait and OTU source families to measure eligible-source and accepted-analysis yield; keep per-bucket counts for distinct programs versus parameter variants.
- [ ] Triage the 386 acquisitions and 646 pending leads into a per-bucket ledger with explicit source-family merges and rights/hold decisions; expand source discovery until a credible 1,000–2,000 potential-task pool exists.
- [ ] Only after that pool gate, run a **separately authorized**, small, budget-capped input-generation/TaskForge pilot and measure cost per *accepted* candidate. Explicitly accounted-for pilots (including the 20-bundle experiment) cost $1.3856368, **not** a certified account total. The working GLM route (2026-11-23) removes an endpoint blocker, not source/validation gates. The user's planning target is about **$100 for ~1,000 candidates**, with the previous **$10 hard ceiling for three-record prompt experimentation**; neither authorizes a full wave.
- [ ] Define and verify the RL Atlas handoff contract, then submit only Stage 60-accepted, rights-cleared tasks; update this issue with submitted counts and evidence.

## Evidence and related work

- Private source snapshots: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin4sc/taskforge/source-corpora/open-biology/` (`gtn-source-files-v1/`, `zenodo-independent-source-files-v1/`, `zenodo-independent-round3-acquired-v4/`, `zenodo-independent-round4-acquired-v3/`, `staged-386-byte-overlap-v1/`). These are **archives/audits**, not training or solver input roots.
- Three-program planning, independent references and controls: `.../open-biology/rlvr-ideat-three-v1/` (private; separate authoring and reference records). Private benchmark-overlap audits are isolated outside the source and authoring prefixes and must not enter generator contexts.
- Marin repository notes (some remain **uncommitted** on `science/id-eval-source-intake`): `experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/id_eval_source_intake/BIXBENCH_OPEN_SOURCE_ACQUISITION.md` and `OPENROUTER_IDEAT_DESIGN_AND_COST.md`.
- Prior BioTasks/Harbor tracking [#9257](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9257) concerns a **different, migrated campaign**. Biology eval tracking [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258) is separate from task production.

comments.author: znichols
comments.body:
### 2026-11-23: matched three-arm **actual-source-content** GLM pilot (not profile-only)

The same three previously test-extracted independent Zenodo records were used, with **all bytes** of only these checksum-verified input files in each request: `5600907/01-species_interactions.csv` (253,789 B), `4942915/individualXtraitsXenv.csv` (143,071 B), `4971364/E11_OTUTable.txt` + `E11_SampleMetadata.txt` (100,766 B). No README, infection data, taxonomy, published results, previous model proposals, reference answers or eval material entered the requests. Each record declares CC0 at record level; constituent-file training rights are **not approved**, so this is a private prompt experiment, not a training-source admission.

One call per `(record, arm)` for **objective-first, question-first and answer-first**, nine calls total; one HTTP attempt/call, no repeated old profile-only requests. All nine completed HTTP 200, finish `stop`, and parsed as JSON candidates. They consumed **861,681 prompt tokens** (repeating all input bytes per arm), **8,364 completion tokens**; this is not cost-efficient enough for a 10k-task pipeline. The frozen new requests, source-selection hashes, prompt templates, raw SSE events and usage are under private `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin4sc/taskforge/source-corpora/open-biology/source-content-three-arm-20261123-v1/`.

Independent first-pass source-byte checks (Python stdlib CSV **and** a separate pandas check for the four nonempty answers) found **five empty model answer objects**, **one incorrect interaction-row count**, and **three exact numeric/reference matches**. By arm, exact matches: objective-first **0/3**, question-first **1/3**, answer-first **2/3**. This is a tiny, non-independent sample: matched network answers overlap in the same analysis family, while the remaining correct answer is a simple single-species trait summary. Other candidates use arbitrary subgroups/top-three cutoffs, unverified measurement semantics or incomplete answer contracts. **Zero are promotion-ready**; no new TaskForge tasks, solver trials, Stage 50/60 results or landed tasks. Private review and per-arm reasons: `.../source-content-three-arm-20261123-v1/reviews/independent-first-pass-v1/summary.json` (SHA-256 `06a2c0bdef5667c410fcc99ed6214758474f8e4b33b4ed399164ae00a507ac6a`).

Important prompt flaw: the JSON shape in the common request wrote `"answer_json":{}`, which likely invited five empty copies. This pilot measures **these specific prompts and full-inline-source delivery**, not inherent yield of the three approaches or of GTN/Zenodo. Next version should retain access to the *actual allowlisted files* through an isolated, credential-free read/compute tool instead of re-sending 83k–111k input tokens per arm; require a nonempty computed answer or explicit null; independently run references and evaluate distinct analyses, not raw response counts. Version new requests; do not replay or overwrite these nine.

comments.author: znichols
comments.body:
### Correction to the nine-call report: iterative source extraction is now underway

The initial **nine calls were prompt calibration**, not extraction to exhaustion; treating them as a finished source pilot was my mistake. I subsequently froze a **bounded four-round-per-(record, arm) extraction plan** for the same three allowlisted records and three approaches. Each round requested up to two distinct programs, with the actual selected source rows visible and read-only access to *all selected file rows* via a bounded `read_rows` tool and in-memory source-only SQL. No eval items, published solutions, unselected files or previous private answers were exposed. Own-arm prior questions, not other arms' outputs, are used to discourage repeats. Request/tool/result snapshots are versioned, with failed attempts retained rather than overwritten.

**Attempt accounting:** 3 records × 3 arms × 4 planned rounds = **36 attempted round cells** in addition to the nine calibration calls. A first runner mistakenly allowed the last tool turn to remain open; I cancelled it after 30 unfinished cells, preserved their paid traces and finalized those *without replaying the four already-made turns*. Six fourth-round cells were separately attempted: **33/36** yielded final candidate/no-task responses, while **3/36** reached a hard tool/finalization budget with no final task and retain that failure disposition. Among the 33 final responses, one explicitly said no-task and the rest yielded **63 raw proposals**: 24 interaction, 22 trait and 17 OTU; by arm: 20 objective-first, 22 question-first and 21 answer-first. These are neither 63 independent programs nor 63 reference-verified tasks. Every proposal's model-authored SQL executed successfully against the first source projection; that alone does **not** validate its question, method or answer.

A follow-on source-byte audit caught a **major projection error**, now immutably recorded: the trait CSV uses literal `NA`. The first SQLite tool retained it as text; aggregate functions treated it as zero rather than missing. The source has 44 `NA` for `lma`, 8 for `lwr`, 54 for `leaf_succulence` (other environmental fields also have missing values). Replaying only the already-frozen queries over a corrected NULL projection changes query results for **19/22 trait proposals**; their answers are **quarantined**, not silently patched. The correction snapshot is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin4sc/taskforge/source-corpora/open-biology/source-content-three-arm-trait-na-correction-20261123-v1/summary.json` (SHA-256 `c2faab6b94a1bbf095ce5513aadac8d572ac8f4bff5af98e817c98e28c117e12`). Some interaction answers also contradict their own source-derived counts. The private 36-cell ledger is `.../source-content-three-arm-multiround-review-20261123-v2/summary.json` (SHA-256 `cc4439886d3c9b18834a6859d11618e2673319a55cfbfe848c02bb7f90aaa932`).

**Do not mark any of these buckets fully extracted yet.** Four rounds is a bounded *pass*, not proof of absolute exhaustion. The next gate is a per-proposal scientific/source-rights review, corrected independent reference computations, and analysis-program deduplication. Only then measure marginal **distinct, independently executable** yield by arm and decide whether to extend the plan or stop after recorded no-new-program rounds. Zero new TaskForge, training-cleared or landed tasks.

issues.title: [post-training] First 10k science RL tasks from open biology sources

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

Evaluate ScienceAgentBench Verified for inclusion in Marin’s in-distribution (ID) evaluation policy. The solver uses Pi to write a Python program against supplied scientific data. EvalDash replays the submitted program in a clean environment and grades its output. Verified revises the original 102-task release and retains its task IDs. Our panel covers 101 tasks. Task 78 is recorded as unrun in both conditions. [Verified release](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench#updates) · [Implementation PR #11599](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11599)

The annotation pin is `9c6e96c9`. At that revision, 41 of 102 rows differ from the original annotations, including nine task instructions. The existing Harbor adapter reads the legacy split without pinning the Hugging Face revision. The Marin implementation uses pinned software environments and stages each task’s checksummed data after startup. [Pinned annotations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/tree/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7) · [Harbor adapter](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/630)

Run the same tasks twice per model, once with the authors’ expert knowledge in the prompt and once without it. Report the fraction of tasks passed separately for each condition. Of the 101 eligible tasks, 37 use programmatic checks and 64 require figure comparisons. For the figure tasks, the current panel uses Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct via Venice on OpenRouter. The publisher used GPT-4o-2024-05-13. We send three independent requests per figure, average the scores, and apply the published task threshold. A completed reply missing the score marker contributes zero. A failed request leaves the trial ungraded. [Paper and author protocol](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3)

### Why

The policy question is whether Marin can use this benchmark to track how well cohort models turn a scientific instruction and a dataset into a correct result. The tasks span bioinformatics, computational chemistry, geographical information science, and psychology and cognitive science. Clean replay lets us check the artifact the program actually produces. The paired prompts let us measure how much the same solver benefits from domain guidance, a distinction the authors also studied. [Marin evaluation policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) · [Paper, Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S4.T3)

### Validation

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B results through the official EvalDash path on the revised Pi harness, as of November 23 at 21:25 UTC. The plot column reports **grading coverage**. A full-panel pass rate is pending for each condition. [Deterministic results and sensitivity checks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7083615825)

| Expert knowledge | Programmatic tasks passed | Plot tasks graded | Total tasks graded |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Off | 9/37 (24.3%) | 60/64 | 97/101 |
| On | 11/37 (29.7%) | 6/64 | 43/101 |

- **Grader checks.** On four recovered Qwen outputs, the publisher’s deterministic scorer and the EvalDash adapter agreed on one pass and three failures. Both also passed the reference output for each of the three distinct tasks. Agreement between the substitute plot judge and the publisher’s judge remains unmeasured. Earlier MiniMax pilot grades and the 54 grades from the previous Pi revision are tracked separately. [Same-output grader comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7111004800)
- **Publisher controls.** Across 101 eligible tasks, 29 deterministic references and 58 visual references passed in the reference campaign, four fell below threshold (41, 59, 96, 102), and ten lacked a completed comparison. Task 97 used an extended diagnostic replay allowance. The visual reference campaign predates the current Venice judge route. Report the headline score alongside sensitivity analyses omitting task 41, all four threshold failures, and the two tasks with exposed answers (53 and 58). Keep the released inputs and thresholds for headline results. [Reference evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7045716068)
- **Policy decision.** Finish both Qwen conditions, link the completed EvalDash results, and report coverage, infrastructure failures, sensitivity analyses, and cohort comparisons before making an inclusion recommendation. The paper used different agents and reported best-of-three results. Its published scores are a historical comparison.

### Cost

Each completed model panel covers 202 trials. The configuration allows 60 minutes for solving and 30 minutes for verification, including up to 15 minutes for clean replay. Each sandbox requests 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk. At the November 23 checkpoint above, the two current Qwen visual-run ledgers recorded 177 settled judge calls and about $0.62 charged or reserved. Final judge spend, accelerator-hours and end-to-end runtime are pending.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The Micro210 MBPP+ row `mbppplus/doc:ebde503d6a0649c19b81517f1c688a403e8e3ee7daf087f0ef4a8079ce60d98a` (MBPP `polar_rect`, "convert polar coordinates to rectangular coordinates") scores 0.0 with its own canonical solution. A correct model answer therefore cannot score on this row. The row is in the frozen Micro210 selection (`selection_order` 62), so every Micro210 run counts it as a guaranteed failure.

Reproduce:
1. Build the Micro210 prepared table from the 2026.11.23 policy work (#12069 rebuild) and run its spec-only oracle/NoP gate on MBPP+.
2. Read the gate row for this task: `oracle_reward` 0.0, `nop_reward` 0.0, `environment_exception: true`.
3. Grade the same canonical solution with the frozen `runtime-v4` grader in the same environment: `frozen_grader_oracle_reward` is also 0.0.

Expected: the canonical solution scores 1.0, and a correct answer can pass.

Evidence so far: the row's tests compare `cmath` floating-point results with exact `==`. The building worker reports a 1-ULP mismatch on one hidden MBPP+ input and attributes it to the Python 3.12 complex-number math. That attribution is unverified. The visible test cases pass locally on Python 3.13. Find the failing input and the exact cause (Python version, libm or test-data generation), then either compare with a tolerance in the row's grader or exclude the row from Micro210 in a new policy version. Do not edit the frozen policy in place.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The MBPP+ importer stores the source test program in the task verifier; the grader executes those assertions verbatim. Micro210 hash-pins its prepared table, and [draft PR #12069](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12069) changes only TruthfulQA rows in its staged table, so the MBPP+ failure remains. The canonical `polar_rect` solution passes all three published MBPP/590 assertions on local CPython 3.12; the failing hidden input and Python/libm attribution remain unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`code.py#L105-L130`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/code.py#L105-L130) — packages the source tests.
- [`code_protocol.py#L129-L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/assets/code_protocol.py#L129-L147) — builds the executable test program.
- [`micro210_inputs.py#L87-L96`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1/experiments/evaluation/micro210_inputs.py#L87-L96) — carries verifier resources into prepared rows.
- [`micro210.py#L73-L78`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1/experiments/evaluation/micro210.py#L73-L78) — rejects any unpinned table change.

# Proposed Fix

1. Extract this task from the pinned and staged prepared tables. Run its canonical answer in the `runtime-v4` grader image with assertion-level diagnostics; record the first failing input, actual and expected values, Python version, and math-library environment. Replay that case on 3.12 and 3.13 to distinguish runtime drift from a bad expected value.
2. If the mismatch is only floating-point rounding, replace exact numeric comparisons for this row with explicit tolerances in a new prepared-table build. If the reference is substantively wrong, remove the row and select a replacement under a new policy version. Keep the frozen policy unchanged.
3. Require the canonical answer to score 1.0 and a wrong answer to score 0.0 in the pinned grader environment. Run the MBPP+ oracle/NoP gate and compare row hashes so the policy notes identify every changed benchmark.
4. Fold the result into the active #12069 policy build, alongside the CRUXEval and IFBench corrections already requested on #12060. Publish new immutable public-policy and private-table commits, then pin their commit IDs, sizes, and SHA-256 values in the launcher.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 # Evidence: failing hidden input, cause, and the fix in the new version

**Failing hidden input** (MBPP+ plus-test data, row `mbppplus/doc:ebde503d…`, task 590 `polar_rect`):
`[-30.014161875705714, -29.844058340125226]`. The canonical solution's first result component is
`cmath.polar(complex(x, y))[0]` = `abs(complex)` = **42.326324330254145**, while the test's expected value is
**42.32632433025415** — a 1-ULP difference (the imaginary component `-2.359036256570777` and the second element
`(-2+2.4492935982947064e-16j)` match exactly). Every other hidden input passes.

**Cause — verified, and my earlier CPython-3.12 attribution was wrong.** I reproduced it on Python 3.11.18, 3.12.16,
3.13.18 and 3.14.10 (Debian slim images): all four show the same mismatch, so this is not a 3.12 regression. The
actual mechanism, from CPython `Objects/complexobject.c` (`_Py_c_abs` → `hypot(z.real, z.imag)`):

- `abs(complex)` / `cmath.polar` call **libm `hypot`**. On glibc (Debian), `hypot(-30.014161875705714,
  -29.844058340125226)` returns `42.326324330254145` (verified by calling libm `hypot` through ctypes).
- CPython's **`math.hypot`** does not call libm for two arguments; its own correctly-rounded implementation returns
  `42.32632433025415` for the same pair.
- On macOS, libm `hypot` returns `...15` as well, so the same code agrees there. The MBPP+ expected values
  (`inputs`/`results` arrays baked into the test program) were evidently generated in such an environment, so the
  baked expected value carries `...15` while the Linux runtime computes `...145`.

**Why the row scores 0 rather than near-1:** the embedded evalplus assertion would normally tolerate this —
`assertion(out, exp, atol)` upgrades `atol` to 1e-6 when `is_floats(exp)` — but `is_floats` only recognized flat
`list[float]`/`tuple[float]`. The expected structure here is `((float, float), complex)` (polar_rect returns a
tuple containing a complex), so `is_floats` returned False, the tolerance never applied, and the comparison fell to
exact `==`. ("The visible tests pass on 3.13" holds because the visible MBPP test inputs — e.g. `(3, 4)` — have
exactly-representable results; the defect only bites on the hidden plus-test input above.)

**Fix shipped in the 2026.11.23 rebuild (PR #12069 branch), option (a) — tolerance in the row's grader, selection
unchanged:** the new version's build applies a row-data patch to the MBPP+ embedded test program (#12159, recorded
in each row's grader-provenance label and the policy's `row_data_patches`):

- `is_floats` additionally recognizes `complex` leaves and nested numeric structures (bools still excluded;
  flat-float verdicts unchanged), and
- the assertion compares with a structure-aware fallback (`np.isclose` per leaf, `rtol=1e-07, atol=1e-6` as before)
  because `np.allclose` cannot build an array from the ragged `(tuple, complex)` shape.

With the patch, this row's canonical solution grades 1.0, a NoP answer still grades 0.0, and the other 9 selected
MBPP+ rows grade identically (their expected structures are flat floats, for which the two guards agree). The fix
is scoped to the embedded test program of the new version; the frozen `2026.11.20-together` policy is untouched.

issues.body:
We are targeting an update to our post-training eval policy on November 30th, 2026\. The new policy will focus on improving coverage over key capabilities, especially factuality and math/science reasoning. The purpose of this issue is to invite the community to provide feedback on the listed evals and suggest changes to our implementations.

## Changes to In-Distribution Benchmarks

The tables below list the major changes to our the in-distribution benchmark composition.

* Benchmarks slated for **removal** will be taken out of the policy with high probability,
* Benchmarks flagged for **changes** need some repair to make them work on more recent versions of main,  
* Benchmarks marked as **potential additions** have draft implementations and may be included in the next round.

We will select our in-distribution benchmarks to collectively cover the capabilities necessary for Mochi to do well on our out-of-distribution benchmarks (listed below). Beginning in 2027, we hope to make this process more data-driven, but for the Nov 30 policy, we will select ID benchmarks based on:

1. Our assessment of each benchmark’s quality and appropriateness for hillclimbing,  
2. Whether an eval can be run reliably in our eval infrastructure,  
3. The resource cost of running the eval,  
4. The wall clock time of running the eval,  
5. Coverage over our out-of-distribution benchmarks,  
6. Whether we find eval contamination in our training data.

In the policy announcement on Nov 30, we will explain why particular evaluations were included or excluded. Our full set of in-distribution evals must run in no more than 24 hours for Mochi, and our eval lite subset used for model development must run in no more than 3 hours.

The proposed changes favor more recent evaluations (which have a smaller chance of contamination and reflect modern capability priorities) while increasing implicit weight on scientific tasks. This includes the addition of a number of benchmarks specifically targeting scientific knowledge and reasoning. New core capability benchmarks target factuality (SimpleQA Verified, FACTS Parametric/Grounding), instruction following (MultiChallenge) and realistic long context tasks (LongBench v2). We have not significantly changed the set of agentic evaluations in this round and will instead focus on reliable, performant implementations of our existing evals, with a few exceptions.

## Changes to Out-of-Distribution Benchmarks

Our previous eval policy listed AAII v4.3, Terminal Bench Science v0.1 and DeepSWE v1.1 as out-of-distribution benchmarks. We largely retain this set of evals, with some changes, notably the inclusion of LAB-Bench v2.

Below, we list the full set of evals we consider out of distribution. As a reminder, we do not run these evaluations until the completion of a Marin post-training round and do not look at any individual tasks. The single exception to this rule is the evals team that implements the public subsets of these evaluations for us to report. The evals team does not share any data from the implementation testing with the training team and will protect any data from testing runs from Marin’s training engineers and their agents.

### Public Out of Distribution Benchmarks

* AAII v4.3 and v5.0  
  * Terminal Bench Science v0.1  
  * Terminal Bench 4.0  
  * SciCode  
  * AA-LCR v1.1  
  * HLE Diamond  
  * AutomationBench-AA (public Zapier subset)  
  * AA-Omniscience v1.1 (public subset)  
  * GDPval-AA v2  
* LAB-Bench 2

## Changes to Comparison Models

Mochi belongs to a different weight class from Snowball and its competitor set needs to update accordingly. We are tentatively scoping a four-tier comparison set:

**Tier 0**: Existing Marin models (currently, Snowball)  
**Tier 1**: Strong models in a smaller weight class where Mochi should be competitive.  
**Tier 2**: A collection of peer models from other open providers.  
**Tier 3**: Strong models in Mochi’s weight class that roughly represent the open frontier.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 Implementation notes on the listed evals and comparison models, checked against `main` at `6081e9b` and the open PRs' current heads. Items 1-4 can change a model comparison.

1. **Thinking-off does not reach 8 of the 12 external comparison models.** Protocols express thinking only as `enable_thinking`. In the linked repositories' chat templates, `enable_thinking=false` renders the same prompt as no kwargs for Muse Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+, Solar Open 2, Mistral Large 4, Beam 1.0, Inkling 2 Small and GLM 5.3 Flash. A catalog entry can map thinking-off to another kwarg ([evaluation.py#L157-L160](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L157-L160)), but only Glimmer has an entry. Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Mistral Large 4, Beam and GLM 5.3 Flash have no setting that turns reasoning off. MRCR, IFBench and CRUXEval grade `reasoning + "\n\n" + content` ([response.py#L31-L32](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/response.py#L31-L32)), so MRCR scores 0 for any reply with reasoning (it must start with the nonce, [long_context.py#L36-L40](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/long_context.py#L36-L40)), and one reasoning line can turn an IFBench strict pass into 0 (key 296, `format:no_whitespace`). The 2,048-token caps of CRUXEval and SimpleQA Verified non-thinking and the 4,096 cap of LongBench v2 non-thinking can cut these models off mid-reasoning. Smallest fix: `thinking_off_template_kwargs: {reasoning_effort: none}` for Command A+, Solar Open 2 and Inkling; grade the final answer on thinking-off selections for the rest (#10828, third item); report which rows ran with reasoning. The new catalog entries also need reasoning parsers for these models' markers, because the scorers' inline fallback strips only `</think>` and `<|end_think|>`.

2. **Gemma 4 31B.** The link is the pretrained `google/gemma-4-31B`, which has no chat template. The instruction-tuned `google/gemma-4-31B-it` defaults to thinking off. SuperGPQA, GenomeQA, EconEvals, MultiChallenge and ARC-AGI-2 (#12149) send empty `chat_template_kwargs` (for example [supergpqa.py#L49](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/supergpqa.py#L49)), so Gemma would answer them without reasoning while every other listed model reasons by default. Fix: serve the -it model and set `enable_thinking: true` on those five.

3. **WinoGrande and TruthfulQA MC2 contexts reach the model without BOS.** `encode_pair` encodes non-empty contexts with `add_special_tokens=False` and sends token ids ([likelihood.py#L68-L80](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/likelihood.py#L68-L80)). When I rescored gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's October campaign requests with `<bos>` added, WinoGrande accuracy rose 4.97 points [1.26, 8.68] and MC2 6.26 [3.24, 9.36]. Gemma 4's tokenizer adds no special tokens on encode, so `add_special_tokens=True` would not help. Prefixing `bos_token_id` when the chat template writes `bos_token` covers Gemma 4, Snowball, Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+ and Mistral Large 4. This is #10828's BOS item.

4. **MMLU-Pro** sends the five worked examples in one user message, and the scorer reads the first `answer is (X)` ([choices.py#L23-L28](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/choices.py#L23-L28)), which can be the model's answer to the first example. On the two Grug checkpoints of #11981 (a merged checkpoint and a Snowball RL step) this gives 41.3% and 28.8%, against 74.5% and 75.5% with the examples as turns. Other models are not measured.

5. **GLM-5.3-Flash judges PHYSICS-Verified** ([evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92)) **and IMO-ProofBench (#11967)**, and it is a Tier 3 comparison model, so it would grade its own answers. The gpt-oss-120b judge used elsewhere avoids that.

6. **OlympiadBench** grades the first `\boxed` in reasoning plus answer, and an empty extraction skips the judge ([olympiad.py#L43-L65](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/olympiad.py#L43-L65), [main.py#L52-L53](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/main.py#L52-L53)). The trial policy's smoke run recorded 62 empty extractions in 200 Qwen3.6 attempts (72cd9f8). This is #10828's third item.

7. **ChemBench (#11831):** the prompt's example allows a "comma- or space-separated list" (the next sentence asks for commas), but the answer regex accepts only commas ([chembench.py#L26-L29](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2abdd2c89614aa91b55da1363d415007e3930282/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/chembench.py#L26-L29)). Written with spaces, the correct letters score 0 on all 394 rows that have more than one correct letter; with commas they pass all 2,542 multiple-choice rows.

8. **DS-1000:** see the note on #12147.

<details><summary>Reproduce 1 and 7</summary>

Item 1 (`huggingface_hub`, `transformers`; Qwen 3.8 is a control that honors the flag):

BixBench verification fails before grading because a provider credential reaches the task environment instead of the Shellbox model relay. All 10 BixBench attempts in the SFT527 Micro210 evaluation `.137` failed with no verifier result.

Reproduce:
1. Use runtime `4a256ca776d8c8f10802ca372034b4935d8e1f59` and the frozen GLM-5.3-Flash Micro210 policy `open-athena/micro210-policy@fa38e3eacc25137c9febe898119f08d65cc5ce88/policy.json`.
2. Select a BixBench task from `open-athena/micro210-prepared-tasks@d8fa0e259ae63b1978388b20a17f72036642dd05`. Configure the judge credential on the host through Iris secrets.
3. Run its original Harbor verifier. `Verifier.verify` merges the verifier environment and calls `resolve_env_vars`; `validate_task_environment` rejects `OPENAI_API_KEY`:

```text
ValueError: Provider credentials must remain on the host; use a Shellbox model relay: OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Expected: verifier judge calls use the Shellbox model relay. The provider credential stays on the host. The task gets the relay endpoint and a dummy credential. Keep the credential-forwarding guard enabled.

The guard also exists on current main in `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/utils/env.py`; it is the correct boundary. The fix belongs in verifier connection/environment binding. Add a regression that exercises a judge-backed BixBench verifier through the relay and proves that no provider credential enters its task environment.

Related: #11924 records a missing `OPENAI_API_KEY` before relay binding; this run reaches the separate forbidden-provider-credential check. Use one shared relay fix where possible. Ship it with the new Micro210 version tracked in #12060, without changing the frozen policy. The retained error audit is linked from the SFT527 report in #11994.

# Proposed Fix

Attach `judge_connection` before selecting the harness. After restoring `task.toml` and applying task bindings, derive the declared judge model, bind `lowered.judge_connection` to the trial's host model authentication, and rewrite verifier variables with `model_guest_environment`. Pass runtime relay variables only when the task environment declares model access; verify templated and literal verifier endpoints through Harbor's `Verifier.verify`, with the host key absent from guest commands.

[PR #11787](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11787) already implements verifier routing in this runtime, but adds `installed_agent.judge_model`; reconcile its open changes with the connection-based path above before landing this fix. No parallel PR opened against the same runtime.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## Summary

`fetch_file_set()` in `lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py` unconditionally rewrites every file in a FineStore bucket via `atomic_rename()` on every job start, while `FineStoreDirectory` uploads every pre-existing leftover file from persistent `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune/process-0` into the current `tree_hash`'s FineStore bucket. Because `configure_jax_compilation_cache()` runs synchronously before `jax.distributed.initialize()` with no timeout, size cap, or progress logging, multi-million-file stores add `6.5–7 minutes` of startup overhead on healthy nodes and caused 3 separate 64-GPU jobs to fail before compilation on a node with slower small-file XFS writes.

*(This issue tracks the contained fetch/upload fixes; the broader multi-rank autotune uniformity redesign is tracked separately.)*

## Confirmed defects on `main` (`7210b12a88`)

1. **Unconditional full rewrite on every start (`lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py:34-53`):**
   - `fetch_file_set(root, local)` iterates every descriptor in `BlobTables.DESCRIPTORS` and unconditionally stages and renames each file (`atomic_rename()` at `:48` -> `Path.open("wb")` at `:49`), even when `target` already exists on `/cache` with the same size (`BlobDescriptor` already carries `name` and `size` at `lib/finestore/src/finestore/reader.py:200-215`).
2. **Pre-existing host leftovers uploaded into FineStore (`lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py:95-100, 111-116`, `lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py:76, 92-93`):**
   - `compile_cache.py` points global rank 0 (`UPLOADER`) at persistent uncleaned `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune/process-0` (`makedirs(exist_ok=True)`).
   - `FineStoreDirectory.__init__` sets `self._known = fetch_file_set(self._root, local)` (`:76`), and `flush()` uploads `pending = sorted(present - self._known)` (`:92-93`) — pushing every pre-existing local leftover into the current `tree_hash` bucket.
   - Observed remote store sizes: **`2,786,218` logical files** (`168` objects, `246.98 MiB` compressed in object storage) in one `tree_hash` bucket and **`2,786,196` logical files** (`417` objects, `517.47 MiB` compressed) in another — expanding to **`~11 GiB`** on local disk per node at 4 KiB block granularity.
3. **Unbounded, silent pre-init fetch (`lib/iris/src/iris/jax/init.py:279`, `compile_cache.py:116`, `fileset.py:34-53`):**
   - `configure_jax_compilation_cache()` runs before `jax.distributed.initialize()` with no timeout, no file-count or byte cap, and no progress logging after `XLA per-fusion autotune cache: <dir>`.

## Observed impact (3 failed 64-GPU jobs in one night)

- **Healthy nodes:** Rewriting `2.79M` files (`~11 GiB`) per fetcher rank (`process_index % 8 == 0`) runs at ~`7,000 files/s` and takes **`6.5–7 minutes`** before distributed init (`~6 min 38 s` observed across `2,786,218–2,786,492` files / `~11 GiB` per node).
- **Slow-disk node:** On one node whose local `/cache` XFS array writes small files ~10x slower (~`650 files/s`; measured `240,961 -> 265,697` rewritten files in `38 s`, projecting to ~`70 min` for `2.79M` files, with kernel D-state samples in `rename()` / `wchan __flush_work` and `Path.open` / `wchan xfs_buf_lock`), 3 separate 64-GPU jobs failed before compiling:
  1. **Pre-job:** One fetcher rank (`process 8`) logged nothing for `36 min 48 s` after `XLA per-fusion autotune cache:`, until all 63 peer ranks failed on `CoordinationService/RegisterTask` (`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, 30-min deadline).
  2. **Training run:** `process 8` spent `>20 min` inside `fetch_file_set` -> `atomic_rename` (`rename()` / `__flush_work`, `2,786,318` files / `~11 GiB`) while 63 peers waited in JAX init; cancelled before reaching training.
  3. **Diagnostic run:** `process 8` rewrote at ~`650 files/s` (`~265k / 2.79M` in `7.5 min`, ~`70 min` projected vs. the 30-min `RegisterTask` deadline); cancelled before reaching training.

## Expected / requested fixes

1. **Skip-if-present in `fetch_file_set()` (`fileset.py:34-53`):** Before staging and `atomic_rename()`, check whether `target` already exists locally with matching `descriptor.size` (and/or digest/metadata), avoiding millions of redundant small-file writes on warm `/cache` volumes.
2. **Bound and instrument the fetch (`compile_cache.py:116`, `fileset.py:34-53`):** Add a configurable timeout, a max file-count / byte cap, and periodic progress logging (elapsed time, files written/skipped, files/s) so a slow node or bloated store fails fast and visibly instead of hanging silently until `RegisterTask` expires (and raise rather than silently falling back to an inconsistent partial folder).
3. **Stop uploading pre-existing leftovers (`fileset.py:76, 92-93`, `compile_cache.py:113-114`):** Seed `FineStoreDirectory._known` with all files already present in `local` at `__init__` (not only the fetched set) so `flush()` uploads only files newly created during the current run, and skip starting the uploader thread when `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests in `lib/finestore/tests/test_fileset.py` and `lib/iris/tests/` (e.g. `test_jax_init.py` or a new `test_jax_compile_cache.py`) verify:
  1. `fetch_file_set()` skips rewriting existing matching files (zero `atomic_rename` calls on a warm repeat fetch) while still writing missing or size-mismatched files.
  2. Fetch timeout, max file-count / byte cap, and periodic progress logs trigger cleanly and fail loudly on breach.
  3. `FineStoreDirectory` seeded against a directory with pre-existing leftover files uploads `0` pre-existing files on `flush()`, uploading only files created after `__init__`.
  4. `configure_jax_compilation_cache()` does not start the `FineStoreDirectory` uploader thread when `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`.

## Related issues

- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11793
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11909
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11775
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11917

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

## Research

[`fetch_file_set()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7210b12a8864daaace69a519267960576a8eb0f4/lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py#L34-L53) rewrites every descriptor, and [`FineStoreDirectory`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7210b12a8864daaace69a519267960576a8eb0f4/lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py#L64-L93) only excludes fetched paths from later uploads. The node-local directory persists across builds, while [`configure_jax_compilation_cache()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7210b12a8864daaace69a519267960576a8eb0f4/lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py#L91-L116) fetches synchronously before distributed initialization. The existing [fetch wrapper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7210b12a8864daaace69a519267960576a8eb0f4/lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py#L138-L145) also treats an I/O failure after partial materialization as a cold start. I found no open PR for this path.

## Proposed Fix

This needs a bounded fetch contract across FineStore and Iris, with these implementation steps:

1. Give `fetch_file_set()` explicit file-count, logical-byte, deadline, and progress settings. Count every descriptor, including skipped files; check limits before writing, report elapsed time and written/skipped counts periodically, and raise a specific error on breach. Skip an existing regular file only when its recorded size matches. Namespace the local directory by `tree_hash` (or verify a stored digest) so a same-size file from another build cannot be mistaken for a match. A deadline checked between files cannot interrupt one blocked XFS operation; enforce the startup deadline outside the fetch worker if the timeout must cover blocked I/O.
2. Seed `FineStoreDirectory`'s known paths from the local directory after fetching and before starting its thread. Its first and later flushes should publish only files created after construction. Treat fetch-limit and timeout errors as startup failures, including when a partial directory remains; keep any separate policy for an object-store outage explicit.
3. In Iris, parse `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0` before choosing an uploader or fetcher and avoid creating the synchronizer in that mode. Pass the fetch settings from one documented configuration point.
4. Add temp-directory FineStore regressions for warm reuse, missing and mismatched files, both caps, timeout, progress, and leftover exclusion. Add Iris coverage for level 0 and failure propagation. Then run affected safe tests, required formatting and lint review, and publish a PR with `Fixes #11925`.

🤖 # Research

`marin.scaling_laws` has IsoFLOP fitting but no hinted-accuracy fitter. The [paper's released code](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/tree/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30) supplies per-problem outcomes, model FLOPs, a bounded multi-start joint fit, and both unhinted and two-stage baselines; its two-stage baseline uses BPB on GSM8K reference solutions, whereas this issue asks for Paloma BPB. [#11866](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11866) will produce Marin hint records, and [#11870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11870) will apply these forecasts to the hero ladder; no open PR overlaps the fitter.

**Relevant code**
- [`isoflop_analysis.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/scaling_laws/isoflop_analysis.py#L71-L99) — existing typed scaling records and Paloma metric.
- [`plot.py`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/experiments/forecasting/plot.py#L179-L256) — joint law, optimizer, sigmoid baseline.
- [`two_stage.py`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/experiments/forecasting/two_stage.py#L58-L93) — BPB power law and accuracy fit.
- [`data/results/README.md`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/data/results/README.md) — released per-problem data and seed rules.

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a pure `marin.scaling_laws.hinted_accuracy` module with typed per-problem outcomes (`model`, `seed`, `problem_id`, `method`, `hint`, `rollout`, `passed`, training FLOPs) and a separate per-model BPB input; reject incomplete or mismatched model/hint grids before fitting.
2. Fit one bounded six-parameter law per hint method with multi-start least squares on equally weighted model/hint accuracy cells, using `C = log10(training FLOPs)` and `H = 0` for forecasts; return masking, truncation, and their arithmetic-mean ensemble forecasts alongside the two-parameter unhinted sigmoid and the FLOPs → Paloma BPB → accuracy baseline. Center `C` for optimization and convert the intercept back before comparing published parameters.
3. Bootstrap problem IDs as paired units across models, seeds, hint levels, and methods, retaining all rollouts within each sampled problem; return fixed-seed percentile intervals for each forecast and baseline difference, plus the number of failed or degenerate refits.
4. Add behavior tests for known synthetic parameters, held-out forecasts, paired bootstrap intervals, and degenerate grids; reproduce the paper's Delphi parameters and forecasts from its pinned released outcomes, then test the Paloma baseline separately because its BPB input differs from the paper's reference-solution BPB. Wire the #11866 records into this module only after their schema lands; #11870 owns hero-ladder fitting and the go/no-go decision.

## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.
